Uni Hunting Day

A morning at the tide pools with Alice: forage fresh uni straight from the Pacific at Pillar Point, then eat it on the rocks with rice and nori before heading home.

Before You Go

Get Your License

Do this a few days ahead, not the morning of.

Online~$21 each

Buy a California Sport Fishing License

Each of you needs your own. Buy it online at wildlife.ca.gov/Licensing/Fishing or through the CDFW app — it's valid on your phone right away, no need to print anything. Get the 1-day license unless you think you'll forage again this year, in which case the annual (~$65) pays for itself after a few trips.

Buy license →
Bag limit35 per person

Know your limit

The license covers up to 35 sea urchins per person, per day. Between the two of you that's plenty for a fresh-uni feast, with room to spare.

Timing

Pick a Day

You need a "minus tide" for the deep pools to be exposed. Here are the best upcoming weekend windows, pulled from actual NOAA predictions for Half Moon Bay.

Timing tip

Arrive early

Get there 1 to 1.5 hours before the listed low tide time, so you catch the whole outgoing tide instead of just the last few minutes of it.

Packing List

Pack Your Bag

Tools for the hunt, plus everything you need for the feast after.

Hunting gear

What to bring for the hunt

  • Cut-resistant gloves
  • A pry tool (garden hand tiller, flathead screwdriver, or tongs)
  • Kitchen shears and a crab cracker
  • A bucket or mesh bag
  • A cooler with ice packs, left cracked open so urchins can breathe
  • Sturdy water shoes with real grip
  • A headlamp or flashlight, even for a late-afternoon tide
  • A small spoon and tweezers, for cleaning the roe later
Feast ingredients

What to bring for the feast

  • Cooked sushi rice, packed warm in an insulated container
  • Nori sheets
  • Soy sauce, in a small travel bottle
  • A tube of wasabi
  • Pickled ginger, if you like it
  • Sliced scallion or shiso, optional but nice
The Main Event

The Hunt

Pillar Point, Half Moon Bay — about a 15-minute walk from parking down to the tide pools.

Read this first

Stay south of the point

The area near Mavericks to the north is inside the Pillar Point State Marine Conservation Area / Montara State Marine Reserve, where taking anything is illegal. Check the CDFW marine protected area map on your phone before you start, and if you're ever unsure which side of the line you're on, leave it alone.

MPA info →
Park & walk~15 min

Park at Pillar Point, El Granada

Go early on good-tide days — the lot fills up fast. It's about a 15-minute walk from the parking area down to the tide pools.

Map it →
🏖️
Forage · as the tide drops
Gloves on

Work the pools

Gently pry urchins loose with your tool as the tide drops. Purple urchins are the common find here. Collect what you need, well under the 35-per-person limit, and keep them cool in the cracked-open cooler.

Little tip

Heavier means more roe

Urchins that feel heavy for their size usually have more roe inside. A quick weight-check before you commit to prying one loose can save you some effort.

The Payoff

Shuck & Eat

Set up on a dry, flat rock away from the waterline, then build hand rolls right there.

Shucking station

Open the shell

Cut a circle around the mouth on the underside with your shears, drain the liquid, then pry the shell fully open.

Use seawater

Rinse and scoop

Rinse the inside with seawater, not fresh water — fresh water washes out the flavor. Scoop out the five roe lobes with your spoon, picking out any dark bits with tweezers.

Assemble

Build your hand roll

Nori, a scoop of rice, a lobe of fresh uni, a dot of wasabi, a dash of soy. Eat it immediately, right there on the rocks.

Before you leave

Pack out everything

Every shell and scrap goes home with you. This spot is popular, and it's worth keeping it that way.

Before You Go

Good to Know

A few last things worth knowing before you head out.

☎️

Morning-of safety check

Call CDFW's shellfish/biotoxin hotline at 1-800-553-4133 before you leave the house. It's a free recorded line that confirms there's no active domoic acid or red tide advisory for the area. Worth the one-minute call before eating raw seafood.

🗺️

Plan B

If Pillar Point looks crowded or picked-over, Fort Ross on the Sonoma coast is a second legal spot other foragers use, though it's about a 2-hour drive, more of a full-day trip than a quick weekend outing.

📌️

Double-check the boundary

Marine protected area boundaries occasionally shift, so it's worth re-checking the CDFW map the week of your trip.

🌊

Tools for the day

Bring the NOAA tide chart for Half Moon Bay (station 9414131) and the CDFW MPA map pulled up on your phone before you lose signal near the water.
